issues.description: filters='*.exe' breaks the file picker on Linux and macOS where conda has no extension
issues.detail: The conda/mamba/micromamba executables are plain binaries on Linux and macOS. Forcing a '*.exe' filter in the browse dialog means users on the platforms where this feature is most useful cannot even see their conda binary in the picker. This is a cross-platform product. Filter should be platform-aware or simply allow all files.

issues.description: validate_conda substring match flags any binary whose --version output contains 'conda'/'mamba'
issues.detail: Checking `if any(tool in out.decode().lower() ...)` against raw --version output is sloppy. A wrapper script, a path, or an unrelated tool printing one of those substrings passes. Match the program name at a word boundary, or check that the output starts with one of those tokens. Bad taste: a special case dressed as validation.

issues.description: os.access(path, X_OK) is unreliable on Windows and rejects valid executables there
issues.detail: On Windows os.access with X_OK essentially mirrors read access and is not a real executability check, while on POSIX it works. Combined with the '*.exe' filter this whole validate path is platform-confused. Either drop the X_OK gate and rely on the --version probe, or gate it behind a posix-only branch.

issues.description: run_program(...).communicate() leaks the child process if --version hangs and has no timeout
issues.detail: A user-supplied path is executed with no timeout. A misconfigured or wedged binary will block the preferences page validation indefinitely. Use a timeout on communicate() and kill the child on expiry. Small fix, but this is exactly the maintainer-six-years-from-now footgun.

issues.description: Empty-string conda_executable returns True from validate_conda, which is a lie
issues.detail: `if conda_executable == "": return True` papers over the empty-default case to keep the UI quiet. An empty path is not a 'valid Conda executable' — it just means the user hasn't set one. The caller, not the validator, should decide what to do with empty input. Special case that should not exist.

issues.description: kernelspec fallback to custom conda_path silently ignores an unset/invalid configured path
issues.detail: When find_conda() fails and custom_conda is True, the configured conda_path is used with no verification. If the user toggled custom_conda but left the path empty or stale, the code falls through to the not-found error — fine — but if the path is set to garbage, it gets handed to downstream code unchecked. Validate before use, or at minimum log which path was selected.

review.summary: The patch is the right shape: small, scoped to one feature, plumbing in config + a confpage widget + a validator + a fallback in kernelspec. Commit message and UI string are clear. But the validator is sloppy in three ways that matter on a cross-platform tool — Windows-only '*.exe' filter, substring match against --version output, and no timeout on an arbitrary user-supplied binary — and the empty-string-is-valid special case is exactly the kind of taste failure to clean up. NEEDS-WORK: fix the platform handling and tighten validate_conda, then this lands.
